extended.designBasis: No. 2 design of 1847-49: eight columns of 31 figure wheels, the result column plus seven orders of difference, cam-driven addition and carry turned by a hand crank, printing and stereotyping output apparatus; about 3.4 m long, 2.1 m high, 0.5 m deep across the calculating section, about 5 t and about 8,000 parts. Only these figures are taken from the sources; every shape, dimension, name and number here is authored.
extended.viewerNote: The viewer renders one instance per part number, so a figure wheel, a rack or a cam shows once, at its reference occurrence (result column, digit 0, gap 1, cam 1).
extended.featurePositionNote: Feature positions of a repeated part are those of the occurrence named in the interface label; extended.occurrences on an interface is the number of occurrences the BOM gives it.

occurrenceRollup.method: sum over the geometric leaves of the quantities multiplied down each site tree; UK boxed kits counted as stored (boxes)

proposedDefects.brief: about 0.5 % of BOM lines reference a remote revision that is SUPERSEDED
proposedDefects.data: 2 of 316 BOM lines and external references: D-36301 -> urn:plm:es:part:ES-3602 expects 1; UK/3686 -> urn:plm:de:part:D-36019 expects 01
proposedDefects.needs: revision and lifecycle columns on the PLM part tables mapped to atelier:revision and a canonical atelier:lifecycle, an external-reference table per PLM (externer_verweis, reference_externe, referencia_externa, external_ref) in the link graph with atelier:expectedRevision, and a shape failing when the expected revision is in the remote part's superseded revisions

proposedDefects.brief: one whole column group in DE has a lifecycle state that disagrees with its ES frame plate
proposedDefects.data: DE assembly node D-36301 Säulenbaugruppe (all eight columns) is Gesperrt (BLOCKED) while ES-3601 and ES-3602, the plates its column bases bolt to (I2), are Liberado (RELEASED)
proposedDefects.needs: assembly nodes as parts of type ASSEMBLY with a lifecycle, the external-reference table above, and a shape failing when an assembly maps to BLOCKED while a part it references maps to RELEASED

proposedDefects.brief: three FR output parts reference URNs that do not exist
proposedDefects.data: FR3669 -> urn:plm:de:part:D-36091; FR3663 -> urn:plm:es:part:UK/3625; FR3668 -> urn:plm:uk:part:UK/3699
proposedDefects.needs: the external-reference table above and a resolver shape failing when the URN's site segment holds no part of that local id or the site code does not match the id format

proposedDefects.brief: UK fastener kit quantities are in a different unit of issue (boxes of 100 vs each)
proposedDefects.data: bom_line rows of UK/3626, UK/3631 and UK/3634 carry unit_of_issue BX100 with qty 2, 4 and 4; every other row is EA, so a roll-up summing qty understates the UK kit by 990 pieces
proposedDefects.needs: a unit-of-issue column on bom_line mapped to a pack-size literal (atelier:unitOfIssue, atelier:packSize), a roll-up multiplying qty by the pack size, and a shape flagging a child whose consumers (external references in other sites) count in EA

proposedDefects.brief: total mass across sites is off by a constant factor because one site stores grams
proposedDefects.data: FR piece.masse_kg holds grams (extended.massUnit g); FR share 770.4 kg; summed as kilograms the product weighs 775059.3 kg instead of 5463.1 kg
proposedDefects.needs: a mass column in each PLM part table (DE teil.masse_kg, FR piece.masse_kg, ES pieza.masa_kg, UK part.mass_lb) with a @Unit annotation per site mapped to a QUDT unit, atelier:massKg after conversion, and a product-level roll-up over atelier:partOf weighted by BOM occurrences
